iterations.theme: Uvod u svjedočanstvo: neispunjena očekivanja u braku, duhovna borba i brak kao najglasnije evanđelje

sections.subtitle: Umjesto spektakla, poziv na dubinu srca: što govori oltar s brojevima 5 i 2
sections.screenshot_description: Kevin Monette pokazuje prema oltaru i objašnjava značenje brojeva 5 i 2
sections.content:
Kevin Monette, gost iz službe Encounter Ministries, odmah na početku jasno daje do znanja da ova večer neće biti ono što bi publika možda očekivala. Kaže da bi mogao govoriti o **najboljim proročkim riječima** koje je ikada primio ili o **najljepšim ozdravljenjima** kojima je svjedočio. Ipak, ističe da je osjetio kako ih Gospodin te večeri želi povesti „dublje u srce“. Tema večeri je **ozdravljenje u braku** i pitanje kako se čovjek može više suobličiti Kristu da bi to ozdravljenje ušlo u bračni odnos.

Nakon kratkog pokušaja da pozdravi na hrvatskom („Dobro je dan“) i šaljivog pitanja prevoditelju je li dobro izgovorio, Monette okupljene pita jesu li spremni da ih Gospodin te večeri dovede do poniznosti.

Zatim dijeli osobni uvid iz molitve. Dok je molio u crkvi, primijetio je na oltaru jasno istaknute **brojeve 5 i 2** i pitao je Gospodina što time želi poručiti zajednici kojoj taj oltar pripada. Odgovor koji je osjetio glasio je: **„Ono što trebate donijeti je dovoljno.“**

Poruku upućuje osobito onima koji misle da nisu dovoljno daroviti ili da nemaju ono što imaju drugi. Gospodin im, prema Monetteu, poručuje: „Donesi ono što imaš, i to je dovoljno.“ Povezuje to s evanđeoskim dječakom koji je donio **pet kruhova i dvije ribe**. Bog, kaže, želi cijelog čovjeka, ali ne traži ono što čovjek nema. Taj dio je, zaključuje, „Njegov posao“.
sections.subtitle_en: Instead of a spectacle, an invitation to the depth of the heart: what the altar with numbers 5 and 2 says
sections.screenshot_description_en: Kevin Monette points toward the altar and explains the meaning of numbers 5 and 2
sections.content_en:
Kevin Monette, a guest from the ministry Encounter Ministries, makes it clear right at the beginning that this evening will not be what the audience might expect. He says he could speak about the **best prophetic words** he has ever received or about the **most beautiful healings** he has witnessed. Yet, he points out that he felt the Lord that evening wanted to lead them "deeper into the heart." The theme of the evening is **healing in marriage** and the question of how a person can become more conformed to Christ so that this healing might enter into the marital relationship.

After a brief attempt to greet in Croatian ("Dobro je dan") and a humorous question to the translator whether he pronounced it well, Monette asks those gathered if they are ready for the Lord to bring them to humility that evening.

Then he shares a personal insight from prayer. While praying in the church, he noticed on the altar clearly highlighted **numbers 5 and 2** and asked the Lord what He wanted to tell the community to which that altar belongs. The answer he felt was: **"What you need to bring is enough."**

He directs the message especially to those who think they are not gifted enough or that they do not have what others have. The Lord, according to Monette, tells them: "Bring what you have, and that is enough." He connects this with the Gospel boy who brought **five loaves and two fish**. God, he says, wants the whole person, but does not ask for what a person does not have. That part is, he concludes, "His job."

sections.subtitle: Zaključan izvan sobe i bez putovnice: lekcija poniznosti iz prvog tjedna u Hrvatskoj
sections.screenshot_description: Kevin Monette sa smiješkom pripovijeda kako se zaključao izvan hotelske sobe
sections.content:
Monette nastavlja u istom duhu poniznosti i otkriva nekoliko nezgoda s gostovanja. U Hrvatskoj je, kaže, otprilike tjedan dana, a već se u prva tri dana **zaključao izvan hotelske sobe**. Uz osmijeh dodaje da je njegova supruga u tome „potpuno uživala“.

Te su noći morali spavati u župnom stanu. Pomogao im je, kako navodi, **otac Ante iz Zaprešića**, koji je došao po njih.

To nije bila jedina nezgoda. Monette je **izgubio i putovnicu**, koju do trenutka predavanja nije pronašao. Srećom, dan ranije stigla mu je hitna zamjenska putovnica.

Anegdote ne priča samo radi smijeha. Njima uokviruje cijelo izlaganje: dok večeras govori o braku, naglašava, to je za njega i suprugu **i dalje aktivno putovanje**. Ako ikome tijekom večeri padne na pamet da su „sve posložili“, poručuje da se sjeti ovog početka.
sections.subtitle_en: Locked out of the room and without a passport: a lesson in humility from the first week in Croatia
sections.screenshot_description_en: Kevin Monette recounts with a smile how he locked himself out of his hotel room
sections.content_en:
Monette continues in the same spirit of humility and reveals several mishaps from his guest visit. He has been in Croatia, he says, for about a week, and already in the first three days he **locked himself out of his hotel room**. With a smile, he adds that his wife "fully enjoyed" that.

That night they had to sleep in the parish house. They were helped, as he states, by **Father Ante from Zaprešić**, who came to pick them up.

That was not the only mishap. Monette also **lost his passport**, which he had not found up to the moment of the talk. Fortunately, the day before, an emergency replacement passport arrived for him.

He does not tell the anecdotes just for laughs. With them he frames the entire presentation: while speaking tonight about marriage, he emphasizes, for him and his wife that is **still an active journey**. If it crosses anyone's mind during the evening that they have "figured everything out," he tells them to remember this beginning.

sections.subtitle: Od Zaprešića do Beča: tko sjedi u publici i zašto je to neuobičajeno
sections.screenshot_description: Kevin Monette se obraća publici i oduševljeno reagira na podignute ruke
sections.content:
Prije same teme Monette upoznaje publiku nizom pitanja. Najprije pita je li tko bio na **Školi proročke službe u Zaprešiću** prethodnog tjedna i je li im bilo lijepo. Kad odaziv nije dovoljno glasan, na hrvatskom dobacuje „Više!“ i šali se da im inače nitko neće vjerovati.

Predstavlja se kao član službe **Encounter Ministries** i priznaje da ta služba radi „puno uzbudljivih stvari“. Zato ponavlja da je mogao govoriti o proroštvima i ozdravljenjima, ali da je osjetio poziv da večer povede dublje, prema srcu.

Pita i je li tko bio na **Encounter konferenciji u Beču**. Nekolicini prisutnih koji su bili na njegovoj sesiji kaže da će čuti istu priču, ali da „drugi put također pomaže“.

Zatim slijedi niz pitanja o sastavu publike:
- koliko ih je u braku („dobar broj“),
- koliko ih aktivno služi,
- koliko ih služi, a supružnik im nije uključen u službu.

Na odgovore na posljednje pitanje reagira oduševljeno: „Slava Gospodinu! Ovo je prekrasno. Ovo što vi ovdje činite nije uobičajeno.“

Najavljuje da će izlaganje biti **duboko utemeljeno u osobnom svjedočanstvu i u Svetom pismu**. Pripremu govora počeo je prije više od godinu dana, kada je osjetio da mu Gospodin govori: „Vrijeme je da podijeliš ključeve koje sam ti dao kako bi pomogao drugima u njihovim brakovima.“ Večer će, kaže, biti „malo o rastu“.

Obraća se i onima koji nisu u braku te posvećenim osobama. Poziva ih da sadržaj promatraju u kontekstu obitelji, kako bi mogli **zagovarati za bračne parove** u svojim životima.
sections.subtitle_en: From Zaprešić to Vienna: who is sitting in the audience and why that is unusual
sections.screenshot_description_en: Kevin Monette addresses the audience and reacts enthusiastically to raised hands
sections.content_en:
Before the theme itself, Monette gets to know the audience through a series of questions. First, he asks if anyone was at the **School of Prophetic Ministry in Zaprešić** the previous week and if they had a good time. When the response is not loud enough, he calls out in Croatian "Više!" [More!] and jokes that otherwise no one will believe them.

He introduces himself as a member of the ministry **Encounter Ministries** and admits that this ministry does "a lot of exciting things." Therefore, he repeats that he could have spoken about prophecies and healings, but that he felt a call to lead the evening deeper, toward the heart.

He also asks if anyone was at the **Encounter Conference in Vienna**. To the few attendees who were at his session, he says that they will hear the same story, but that "the second time also helps."

Then follows a series of questions about the composition of the audience:
- how many of them are married ("a good number"),
- how many of them actively minister,
- how many of them minister while their spouse is not involved in ministry.

To the answers to the last question he reacts enthusiastically: "Praise the Lord! This is wonderful. What you are doing here is not common."

He announces that the talk will be **deeply rooted in personal testimony and in Sacred Scripture**. He began preparing the talk more than a year ago, when he felt the Lord saying to him: "It is time to share the keys I have given you in order to help others in their marriages." The evening will be, he says, "a little bit about growth."

He also addresses those who are not married and consecrated persons. He invites them to observe the content in the context of family, so that they can **intercede for married couples** in their lives.

sections.subtitle: „Dođi, Duše Sveti“: molitva za omekšana srca
sections.screenshot_description: Kevin Monette sklopljenih ruku vodi uvodnu molitvu Duhu Svetom
sections.content:
Prije svjedočanstva Monette poziva okupljene na molitvu. Nakon razigranog pitanja vole li moliti i potvrdnog odgovora publike, započinje znakom križa i zazivom **„Dođi, Duše Sveti“**.

U kratkoj molitvi priznaje da je Duh Sveti prisutan te ga moli da učini svoje djelo:
- da **uvjeri srca** kojima je to potrebno,
- da ih **omekša**,
- da ih **oblikuje**,
- i da ih **povede bliže svome srcu**.

Molitvu završava u Isusovo ime i ponovnim znakom križa. Time je duhovno uokvirio ono što slijedi: osobnu i ranjivu priču o vlastitom braku.
sections.subtitle_en: "Come, Holy Spirit": prayer for softened hearts
sections.screenshot_description_en: Kevin Monette with folded hands leads the opening prayer to the Holy Spirit
sections.content_en:
Before the testimony, Monette invites those gathered to prayer. After a playful question whether they like to pray and an affirmative answer from the audience, he begins with the sign of the cross and the invocation **"Come, Holy Spirit"**.

In a brief prayer, he acknowledges that the Holy Spirit is present and asks Him to do His work:
- to **convict hearts** that need it,
- to **soften them**,
- to **mold them**,
- and to **lead them closer to His heart**.

He ends the prayer in Jesus' name and with another sign of the cross. With that, he spiritually framed what follows: a personal and vulnerable story about his own marriage.

sections.subtitle: Portland, prsten i snovi: očekivanja mladoženje prije trinaest godina
sections.screenshot_description: Kevin Monette šaljivo opisuje svoja romantična očekivanja od braka
sections.content:
Monette publici zatim daje kontekst predavanja. Prije **13 godina oženio se u Portlandu, u saveznoj državi Oregon**, i bio je, kako kaže, „jako uzbuđen“. Na zaručnički prsten potrošio je gotovo svu životnu ušteđevinu i dodaje da je to bila „ispravna odluka“. Neoženjenima uz smijeh savjetuje da o tome mole, ali da im je to ujedno i savjet.

U brak je, priznaje, ušao s nizom očekivanja koja potom slikovito nabraja:
- **duge noćne razgovore** o svim svojim nadama i snovima,
- suprugu koja se **smije svim njegovim šalama** i hvali njegove uspjehe,
- **duga razdoblja zaljubljenog gledanja u oči**, uz šalu da ime Kevin zapravo znači „zgodan“,
- da će mu se supruga **pridružiti u hobijima**, poput trčanja i vježbanja,
- da će **zajedno stvarati glazbu**, jer je otkrio da supruga ima prekrasan glas,
- i, naravno, **veliku fizičku intimnost**, s medenim mjesecom kao vrhuncem svega toga.

Potom duhovito zaključuje: „I sva moja očekivanja su se ispunila i živjeli smo sretno do kraja života.“ Dodaje da time predaje riječ Josipu, koji će voditi ostatak večeri. Kad vidi zbunjena lica, odmah se ispravlja: „Šalim se. To se nije dogodilo.“
sections.subtitle_en: Portland, ring, and dreams: expectations of a groom thirteen years ago
sections.screenshot_description_en: Kevin Monette humorously describes his romantic expectations of marriage
sections.content_en:
Monette then gives the audience the context of the talk. **13 years ago he got married in Portland, in the state of Oregon**, and was, as he says, "very excited." He spent almost all of his life savings on the engagement ring and adds that it was the "right decision." To the unmarried, with a laugh, he advises them to pray about it, but that it is also his advice to them.

He entered into marriage, he admits, with a series of expectations that he then pictorially lists:
- **long late-night conversations** about all their hopes and dreams,
- a wife who **laughs at all his jokes** and praises his successes,
- **long periods of lovingly looking into each other's eyes**, with a joke that the name Kevin actually means "handsome",
- that his wife would **join him in hobbies**, such as running and exercising,
- that they would **make music together**, because he discovered that his wife has a beautiful voice,
- and, of course, **great physical intimacy**, with the honeymoon as the culmination of all that.

Then he humorously concludes: "And all my expectations were fulfilled and we lived happily ever after." He adds that with this he hands over the floor to Josip, who will lead the rest of the evening. When he sees confused faces, he immediately corrects himself: "I'm joking. That didn't happen."

sections.subtitle: Kad se stvarnost sudari sa snovima: neispunjena očekivanja i „suprotni“ rezultati testa
sections.screenshot_description: Kevin Monette prepričava reakciju svećenika na rezultate testa kompatibilnosti
sections.content:
Stvarnost je, otkriva Monette, izgledala sasvim drukčije. Supruga je željela da nakon vjenčanja **uzme pauzu od služenja**. Ispostavilo se da je ranije imala **ozljedu noge**, pa s njim nije htjela vježbati. Voli pjevati već napisane pjesme, ali joj je **samo stvaranje glazbe izazivalo veliku tjeskobu**.

Najosjetljivije je bilo područje fizičke intimnosti. Supruga je prema njoj osjećala **snažnu odbojnost**, a on tada nije znao zašto. Ono što je, kako su mu govorili, trebalo biti najlakši dio medenog mjeseca, za njih je postalo **najveća poteškoća**.

Monette pita publiku koliko se njih može poistovjetiti s nekim od tih neispunjenih očekivanja. Kad se digne tek nekoliko ruku, uz smijeh dobacuje da „neki od vas lažu“.

Zatim postavlja ključno pitanje: kako se od običnih neispunjenih očekivanja dolazi do **duhovnih komplikacija**? Da bi objasnio „moć neispunjenih očekivanja“, prepričava iskustvo iz priprave za brak. U SAD-u je, kaže, uobičajeno da zaručnici rade **test kompatibilnosti**, jer Crkva želi da budu pripremljeni na ono što ih čeka. Kad su on i supruga s rezultatima sjeli kod svećenika, uslijedila je duga, rječita pauza. Svećenik je zatim rekao: „Pa, vi ste gotovo u svemu postigli suprotne rezultate. Ali ako se budete držali Isusa, valjda će biti dobro.“ Monette priznaje da u tome „ima nešto istine“.
sections.subtitle_en: When reality collides with dreams: unfulfilled expectations and "opposite" test results
sections.screenshot_description_en: Kevin Monette recounts the priest's reaction to the compatibility test results
sections.content_en:
The reality, Monette reveals, looked completely different. His wife wanted him to **take a break from ministry** after the wedding. It turned out that she had previously suffered a **leg injury**, so she did not want to exercise with him. She loves to sing already written songs, but **the very act of making music caused her great anxiety**.

The most delicate was the area of physical intimacy. His wife felt a **strong aversion** toward it, and at that time he did not know why. What, as they had told him, was supposed to be the easiest part of the honeymoon, became for them **the greatest difficulty**.

Monette asks the audience how many of them can identify with any of those unfulfilled expectations. When only a few hands are raised, with a laugh he interjects that "some of you are lying."

Then he asks the key question: how does one go from ordinary unfulfilled expectations to **spiritual complications**? In order to explain the "power of unfulfilled expectations," he recounts an experience from marriage preparation. In the USA, he says, it is customary for engaged couples to take a **compatibility test**, because the Church wants them to be prepared for what awaits them. When he and his wife sat down with the results before the priest, a long, eloquent pause followed. The priest then said: "Well, you have scored opposite results in almost everything. But if you cling to Jesus, I suppose it will be fine." Monette admits that there is "some truth in that."

sections.subtitle: „Potrebno je troje za ljubav“: od bolesnog srca do borbe ili bijega
sections.screenshot_description: Kevin Monette citira blaženog Fultona Sheena o trima osobama u braku
sections.content:
Što se dogodi kada se u brak uđe s mnoštvom neispunjenih nada? Monette odgovor pronalazi u Bibliji i navodi **Izreke 13,12**: „Neispunjena nada čini srce bolesnim.“ Prevoditelj u šali napominje da je riječ o slobodnom prijevodu, što nasmijava i samog gosta.

Posljedice se, objašnjava Monette, ne vide samo izvana nego i iznutra, kao **razočaranje i odbačenost**. Ako se ono što je čovjek očekivao ne dogodi, s tim „mora nešto učiniti“. Može se osjećati iznevjereno ili odbačeno, kao da su mu želje srca ugašene, ili se naći uz osobu koja se nikako ne slaže s njim. To su, naglašava, **prirodne reakcije kada se ti osjećaji ne prinesu Bogu**.

Tu poziva u pomoć **blaženog Fultona Sheena**, nedavno proglašenog blaženim, koji je rekao: **„Potrebno je troje da bi se vodila ljubav, ne dvoje“**: ti, tvoj supružnik i Bog. Sheen dodaje da bez Boga ljudi uspijevaju samo izvući ono najgore jedno iz drugoga.

S Bogom je, prema Monetteu, drukčije. Isus unosi svjetlo u zbunjenost. Može pokazati put, ponuditi veći dar nego što se očekivalo ili osloboditi čovjeka od nečega što mu nije dobro. Kad Isus progovori, stavlja nadu u srce.

Tu misao potkrepljuje **Katekizmom Katoličke Crkve, br. 1608**: da bi se iscijelile rane grijeha, muškarac i žena trebaju pomoć milosti koju im Bog u svojem beskrajnom milosrđu nikada ne uskraćuje. Bez Božje pomoći ne mogu ostvariti jedinstvo života za koje ih je Bog stvorio „u početku“.

Bez te pomoći, objašnjava Monette, supružnici obično reagiraju na dva načina:
- **borba**: kada Bog nije naš zaštitnik, borimo se za kontrolu;
- **bijeg**: povlačimo se i skrivamo, opet radi kontrole.

U braku oba puta vode istom ishodu: **izolaciji i razdvojenosti**.
sections.subtitle_en: "It takes three to love": from a sick heart to fight or flight
sections.screenshot_description_en: Kevin Monette quotes Blessed Fulton Sheen on the three persons in marriage
sections.content_en:
What happens when one enters marriage with a multitude of unfulfilled hopes? Monette finds the answer in the Bible and cites **Proverbs 13:12**: "Hope deferred makes the heart sick." The translator jokingly remarks that this is a loose translation, which also makes the guest himself laugh.

The consequences, Monette explains, are seen not only externally but also internally, as **disappointment and rejection**. If what a person expected does not happen, he "must do something with it." He may feel betrayed or rejected, as if the desires of his heart have been extinguished, or find himself beside a person who does not agree with him at all. Those are, he emphasizes, **natural reactions when those feelings are not brought to God**.

Here he calls to his aid **Blessed Fulton Sheen**, recently beatified, who said: **"It takes three to make love, not two"**: you, your spouse, and God. Sheen adds that without God, people only manage to bring out the worst in each other.

With God, according to Monette, it is different. Jesus brings light into confusion. He can show the way, offer a greater gift than expected, or deliver a person from something that is not good for him. When Jesus speaks, He places hope in the heart.

He supports this thought with the **Catechism of the Catholic Church, no. 1608**: to heal the wounds of sin, man and woman need the help of the grace that God in His infinite mercy never refuses them. Without God's help they cannot achieve the union of their lives for which God created them "in the beginning."

Without that help, Monette explains, spouses usually react in two ways:
- **fight**: when God is not our protector, we fight for control;
- **flight**: we withdraw and hide, again for the sake of control.

In marriage both paths lead to the same outcome: **isolation and separation**.

sections.subtitle: Đavao mrzi brak: laži koje razdvajaju i poziv na potpuno sebedarje
sections.screenshot_description: Kevin Monette naglašava da đavao mrzi brak s gorućom strašću
sections.content:
Monette publici postavlja retoričko pitanje: kome se sviđaju izolacija i razdvojenost? Onome koji je rekao da „nije dobro da čovjek bude sam“ ili onome čije ime na grčkom znači **„razdvajati“**? Kad se većina složi da je riječ o đavlu, gost izgovara jednu od ključnih rečenica večeri: **„Ljudi, đavao mrzi brak.“** Mrzi ga, kaže, „s gorućom strašću“, jer brak predstavlja sve ono što on nije i sve ono što nikada ne može imati. Njegova je misija da krade, ubija i uništava.

U vlastitom braku, otkriva Monette, neprijatelj ih je godinama hranio lažima poput ovih:
- „Vi ste toliko različiti.“
- „Ne znam hoćete li ikada biti sretni.“
- „Je li išta ispalo kako si očekivao?“
- „Možda si donio krivu odluku.“

Pita publiku zvuči li to komu poznato. Upozorava da će đavao učiniti sve kako bi u brakove posijao **sumnju i nesigurnost**. Ako uspije razdvojiti supružnike, oni se udaljuju od samog smisla za koji su stvoreni, a stvoreni su **za ljubav i odnos, za ranjiv i otvoren odnos**.

Tu misao ilustrira anegdotom s vjenčanja. Prijatelji su im napisali čestitku u kojoj je stajalo: „Ako se ikad posvađate, najbolje što možete učiniti je jednostavno se skinuti.“ Iako su vjerojatno htjeli biti duhoviti, Monette poziva da se o tome ozbiljno razmisli. Prvi muškarac i prva žena u raju bili su **potpuno ogoljeni**, a to je bilo **potpuno sebedarje**. Zatim upire pogled u Isusa na križu: ranjenog, ogoljenog, također u potpunom sebedarju.

I u radostima i u kušnjama, zaključuje, za to smo stvoreni: **da druge gledamo i ljubimo te da dopustimo da i nas same netko gleda i ljubi.**
sections.subtitle_en: The devil hates marriage: lies that divide and the call to total self-giving
sections.screenshot_description_en: Kevin Monette emphasizes that the devil hates marriage with a burning passion
sections.content_en:
Monette poses a rhetorical question to the audience: who likes isolation and separation? The One who said that "it is not good for man to be alone" or the one whose name in Greek means **"to divide"**? When the majority agrees that it is the devil, the guest utters one of the key sentences of the evening: **"People, the devil hates marriage."** He hates it, he says, "with a burning passion," because marriage represents everything that he is not and everything that he can never have. His mission is to steal, kill, and destroy.

In his own marriage, Monette reveals, the enemy fed them for years with lies such as these:
- "You are so different."
- "I don't know if you will ever be happy."
- "Did anything turn out the way you expected?"
- "Maybe you made the wrong decision."

He asks the audience if that sounds familiar to anyone. He warns that the devil will do everything to sow **doubt and insecurity** into marriages. If he succeeds in separating the spouses, they move away from the very purpose for which they were created, and they were created **for love and relationship, for a vulnerable and open relationship**.

He illustrates that thought with an anecdote from his wedding. Friends wrote them a greeting card in which it stated: "If you ever get into a fight, the best thing you can do is just get naked." Although they probably wanted to be humorous, Monette invites them to seriously reflect on that. The first man and the first woman in paradise were **completely naked**, and that was **total self-giving**. Then he turns his gaze to Jesus on the cross: wounded, stripped, also in total self-giving.

Both in joys and in temptations, he concludes, we were created for this: **to look at and love others, and to allow ourselves also to be looked at and loved.**

sections.subtitle: Stvoreni iz ljubavi i za ljubav: Katekizam o pozivu svakog čovjeka
sections.screenshot_description: Kevin Monette čita odlomak 1604 Katekizma Katoličke Crkve
sections.content:
Teološki temelj svog izlaganja Monette pronalazi u **Katekizmu Katoličke Crkve, br. 1604**. Čita: „Bog, koji je stvorio čovjeka iz ljubavi, također ga poziva na ljubav.“ To je, prema Katekizmu, **temeljni i urođeni poziv svakog ljudskog bića**, jer je čovjek stvoren na sliku i priliku Boga koji je sam ljubav.

O braku isti odlomak kaže da, budući da ih je Bog stvorio kao muškarca i ženu, njihova uzajamna ljubav postaje **slika apsolutne i nepropadljive ljubavi kojom Bog ljubi čovjeka**. Ta je ljubav u Stvoriteljevim očima „dobra, vrlo dobra“.

Citatom Monette zaokružuje dotadašnju misao: brak nije sporedna stvar u duhovnom životu. Upravo u njemu ljudska ljubav postaje odraz Božje ljubavi prema čovjeku.
sections.subtitle_en: Created out of love and for love: the Catechism on the vocation of every human being
sections.screenshot_description_en: Kevin Monette reads passage 1604 of the Catechism of the Catholic Church
sections.content_en:
Monette finds the theological foundation of his presentation in the **Catechism of the Catholic Church, no. 1604**. He reads: "God who created man out of love also calls him to love." That is, according to the Catechism, **the fundamental and innate vocation of every human being**, because man is created in the image and likeness of God who is love Himself.

About marriage the same passage says that, since God created them male and female, their mutual love becomes **an image of the absolute and unfailing love with which God loves man**. That love is in the Creator's eyes "good, very good."

With this quotation Monette rounds off his thought so far: marriage is not a secondary matter in spiritual life. It is precisely in it that human love becomes a reflection of God's love for man.

sections.subtitle: „Ja sam strpljiv”: prva deklaracija ljubavi
sections.screenshot_description: Kevin Monette objašnjava da strpljivost nije dugo čekanje, nego stav srca
sections.content:
Nakon čitanja odlomka iz Prve poslanice Korinćanima 13, Kevin Monette prelazi na prvi od šest „ključeva” ljubavi koje je za tu večer pripremio: **ljubav je strpljiva**. Budući da se sve prevodi, gost publiku poziva da izgovara ono što kaže prevoditelj. Uz šalu dodaje: „Što god on kaže. Oprostite ako nije točno.”

Zatim slijedi prva deklaracija. Okupljeni naglas izgovaraju: **„Ja sam strpljiv.”** Monette ih poziva da zatvore oči i osluhnu kako ta rečenica zvuči u njima. Tu misao ponavlja kroz cijelo izlaganje: osobine ljubavi koje „ne sjedaju”, kod kojih čovjek osjeti nelagodu dok ih izgovara, vjerojatno su upravo područja na kojima Duh Sveti želi raditi.

Odmah otklanja i čest nesporazum. Strpljivost prema njegovim riječima **ne znači čekati „jako, jako, jako dugo”** dok se ljubav jednoga dana sama ne pojavi u domu. „Strpljivost ima sve veze s vašim stavom”, naglašava gost. Strpljivost tako postaje unutarnja postavljenost prema drugome, a ne pasivno odbrojavanje vremena.
sections.subtitle_en: "I am patient": the first declaration of love
sections.screenshot_description_en: Kevin Monette explains that patience is not waiting for a long time, but an attitude of the heart
sections.content_en:
After reading the passage from the First Letter to the Corinthians 13, Kevin Monette moves on to the first of the six "keys" of love that he prepared for that evening: **love is patient**. Since everything is being translated, the guest invites the audience to speak what the translator says. With a joke, he adds: "Whatever he says. Sorry if it's not accurate."

Then follows the first declaration. Those gathered say aloud: **"I am patient."** Monette invites them to close their eyes and listen to how that sentence sounds within them. He repeats that thought throughout the entire presentation: the characteristics of love that "don't sit well," where a person feels discomfort while uttering them, are probably precisely the areas where the Holy Spirit wants to work.

He immediately clears up a frequent misunderstanding as well. Patience according to his words **does not mean waiting "very, very, very long"** until love one day appears on its own in the home. "Patience has everything to do with your attitude," the guest emphasizes. Patience thus becomes an inner posture toward the other, and not a passive counting down of time.

sections.subtitle: Pet jezika ljubavi: zašto pobjeđuje kvalitetno vrijeme
sections.screenshot_description: Gost opisuje supružnike koji listaju mobitele na suprotnim krajevima kauča
sections.content:
Kako bi pokazao što znači strpljivost kao stav, Monette se poziva na poznati okvir **Pet jezika ljubavi** koji je dr. Gary Chapman objavio devedesetih godina. Okvir opisuje pet načina na koje ljudi daju i primaju ljubav:

- **riječi potvrde**
- **kvalitetno vrijeme**
- **fizički dodir**
- **djela služenja**
- **primanje darova**

Gost navodi da je posljednjih godina čitao istraživanja o jezicima ljubavi i pita publiku koji je od njih najčešći. Iz dvorane stižu odgovori „dodir” i „kvalitetno vrijeme”. Točan je drugi: **kvalitetno vrijeme**.

Razlog Monette vidi u kulturi iz koje dolazi. „Barem mi Amerikanci imamo kulturu: idemo, idemo, idemo”, kaže. Zatim postavlja izravno pitanje: što ako ljubav u braku ne osjećamo zato što se u njemu zapravo **ne pojavljujemo**? Pritom misli na stvarnu prisutnost. Slika koju opisuje mnogima je poznata: dvoje supružnika sjedi na suprotnim krajevima kauča i svatko lista svoj mobitel. To, kaže, nije kvalitetno vrijeme. Ide i korak dalje: ni zajednički rad na nekom projektu nije ispunjenje kvalitetnog vremena.
sections.subtitle_en: The Five Love Languages: why quality time wins
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest describes spouses scrolling on their phones at opposite ends of the couch
sections.content_en:
In order to show what patience as an attitude means, Monette refers to the well-known framework **The 5 Love Languages** that Dr. Gary Chapman published in the nineties. The framework describes five ways in which people give and receive love:

- **words of affirmation**
- **quality time**
- **physical touch**
- **acts of service**
- **receiving gifts**

The guest states that in recent years he has been reading research on love languages and asks the audience which of them is the most common. From the hall come answers "touch" and "quality time." The second is correct: **quality time**.

Monette sees the reason in the culture he comes from. "At least we Americans have a culture of: go, go, go," he says. Then he asks a direct question: what if we do not feel love in marriage because we do not actually **show up** in it? By that he means real presence. The picture he describes is familiar to many: two spouses sitting on opposite ends of the couch and each scrolling through their own phone. That, he says, is not quality time. He goes a step further: not even working together on some project is the fulfillment of quality time.

sections.subtitle: Gledati u istom smjeru nije dovoljno: supružnik treba biti viđen
sections.screenshot_description: Kevin Monette govori da se kvaliteta zajedničkog vremena mjeri time koliko se supružnik osjeća viđenim
sections.content:
Monette zatim kritički razmatra misao koju je, kako kaže, mnogo puta čuo u opisima braka. Pripisuje je jednom francuskom autoru: **ljubav se ne sastoji u tome da gledamo jedno u drugo, nego da zajedno gledamo prema van, u istom smjeru**. Priznaje da to zvuči odlično jer odiše jedinstvom i timskim radom. Sam je, podsjeća, na početku braka želio da mu se supruga pridruži u svemu.

U tome ipak vidi problem. Ako je to glavni fokus, ljubav je stalno usmjerena prema van, a supružnik treba **primiti** ljubav. Gost ne umanjuje vrijednost karitativnog djelovanja prema drugima i kaže da je ono „jako važno”. Ipak, za pravo kvalitetno vrijeme u braku drugoga treba promatrati i **vidjeti**. Kvalitetu tog vremena, smatra on, mjeri to koliko se supružnik osjeća viđenim, odnosno koliko je on **prvi i redovito izravni primatelj naše ljubavi**.

Tu misao povezuje s načelom svoje zajednice. U Encounter Ministries kažu da **svako plodno služenje proizlazi iz identiteta**. Zato polaznici, prije nego što ih se uči proricati ili moliti za bolesne, cijelo tromjesečje provode u razgovoru s Bogom, u iskustvu da ih On vidi i poznaje. Tek ih se iz tog mjesta oprema da liječe bolesne, uskrisuju mrtve i čine „sve ostale prekrasne stvari”. Brakovi su, prema gostu, pozvani na isti obrazac: **„Mi ljubimo jer je On prvi ljubio nas.”**
sections.subtitle_en: Looking in the same direction is not enough: the spouse needs to be seen
sections.screenshot_description_en: Kevin Monette says that the quality of shared time is measured by how much the spouse feels seen
sections.content_en:
Monette then critically considers a thought that, as he says, he has heard many times in descriptions of marriage. He attributes it to a French author: **love does not consist in looking at each other, but in looking together outward in the same direction**. He admits that sounds great because it exudes unity and teamwork. He himself, he recalls, at the beginning of marriage wanted his wife to join him in everything.

Yet he sees a problem in that. If that is the main focus, love is constantly directed outward, and the spouse needs to **receive** love. The guest does not diminish the value of charitable activity toward others and says that it is "very important." Still, for true quality time in marriage the other person needs to be observed and **seen**. The quality of that time, he believes, is measured by how much the spouse feels seen, that is, how much they are **the first and regularly direct recipient of our love**.

He connects that thought with a principle of his community. At Encounter Ministries they say that **all fruitful ministry flows from identity**. That is why participants, before being taught to prophesy or pray for the sick, spend an entire trimester in conversation with God, in the experience that He sees and knows them. Only from that place are they equipped to heal the sick, raise the dead, and do "all the other wonderful things." Marriages are, according to the guest, called to the same pattern: **"We love because He first loved us."**

sections.subtitle: Zaboravljeni stih: godina dana za razveseljavanje supruge
sections.screenshot_description: Prevoditelj čita Ponovljeni zakon 24,5 nakon što je pronašao stih
sections.content:
Monette publiku upućuje na stih koji je, kako priznaje, „promašio u svom čitanju Biblije”: **Ponovljeni zakon 24,5**. Dok prevoditelj traži mjesto u hrvatskom izdanju, gost ga čita na engleskom. Nakon kratke zabune oko poglavlja prevoditelj pronalazi stih i čita ga: novovjenčani muž neka ne ide u vojsku i neka mu se ne nameće nikakva služba, nego neka bude oslobođen i ostane kod kuće godinu dana **da razveseljuje ženu koju je doveo**.

„Zamislite kako bi izgledali naši brakovi da uzmemo punu godinu dana na početku braka samo da razveseljujemo svog supružnika”, kaže gost. Na pitanje je li on to učinio odgovara bez okolišanja: „Naravno da nisam.”

Želio je, kaže, dokazati da je vrijedan muž, pa se zaokupio time da bude stalno zaposlen:

- prihvatio je promaknuće i radio dulje na poslu,
- kupili su kuću, a on je stalno kupovao stvari za nju,
- nabavili su štene, a onda se pokajali što su ga nabavili,
- i „nekako” se vratio vođenju službe.

Upravo je služba postala **velik izvor napetosti**. Ulaganje u nju donosilo je mnogo ploda, pa je ulagao još više. Supruzi je pritom govorio: „Zašto si tako tužna? I ti bi to trebala raditi.” Nije shvaćao da je i njoj samoj trebalo služenje. Trebala joj je ljubav i pažnja onih koji su joj najbliži, i to **strpljiva ljubav koja može jednostavno biti s njom** kad se osjeća izgubljeno.
sections.subtitle_en: A forgotten verse: one year for cheering up one's wife
sections.screenshot_description_en: The translator reads Deuteronomy 24:5 after finding the verse
sections.content_en:
Monette directs the audience to a verse that, as he admits, he "missed in his reading of the Bible": **Deuteronomy 24:5**. While the translator looks for the place in the Croatian edition, the guest reads it in English. After brief confusion about the chapter, the translator finds the verse and reads it: a newly married man shall not go out with the army and no public duty shall be imposed on him, but he shall be free and stay at home for one year **to bring cheer to the wife he has taken**.

"Imagine what our marriages would look like if we took a full year at the beginning of marriage just to bring cheer to our spouse," the guest says. To the question of whether he did that, he answers without beating around the bush: "Of course I didn't."

He wanted, he says, to prove that he was a worthy husband, so he preoccupied himself with being constantly busy:

- he accepted a promotion and worked longer hours at work,
- they bought a house, and he was constantly buying things for it,
- they got a puppy, and then regretted getting it,
- and "somehow" he returned to leading ministry.

It was precisely ministry that became **a major source of tension**. Investing in it brought much fruit, so he invested even more. To his wife, he would say: "Why are you so sad? You should be doing this too." He did not realize that she herself needed ministry. She needed the love and attention of those closest to her, and specifically **patient love that can simply be with her** when she feels lost.

sections.subtitle: „Aktivator” koji je često nestrpljiv: kad se snage iz službe obiju o brak
sections.screenshot_description: Gost citira sestru Miriam: „Nisi problem koji treba popraviti, nego osoba koju treba ljubiti”
sections.content:
Monette iskreno priznaje da strpljiva prisutnost nije njegov prirodni način davanja ljubavi. Voli rješavati probleme, riskirati i isprobavati nove stvari. Kao potvrdu navodi rezultate testova osobnosti raširenih u SAD-u. Na testu Strength Finders njegova je najjača osobina **Aktivator**, uz opis „često je nestrpljiv”. Na testu Working Genius ističu se **Tenacity i Galvanizing**. Kad je prevoditelj zapeo na tim izrazima, gost je zatražio pljesak za njega i sam ih „preveo”: „Želim pokrenuti stvari i pokrenuti vas zajedno sa mnom. A ako netko nije spreman krenuti, jednostavno idem onima koji jesu.”

U službi su to, kaže, sjajne osobine. One su znak evangelizatora, onoga kojeg u njegovoj zajednici zovu „žeteocem”, a Crkvi takvih ljudi treba. **U braku se međutim ne može otići nekome drugome tko je spremniji.** Što je više uspijevao kao profesionalni službenik, to je više stvarao ozračje u kojem su se kod supruge produbljivale **rane odbačenosti i napuštenosti**. Ozračje doma oblikovalo je sve što je radio izvan njega, s porukom „mi idemo brzim tempom”. Vrijeme sa suprugom često se svodilo na dijagnosticiranje: kako da te popravimo i dovedemo do naše brzine?

Gost zatim pita koliko je prisutnih nedavno bilo u Međugorju na susretu John Paul II Healing Centera, nakon čega se spominje i ime Boba Schutza. Navodi rečenicu koju često ponavlja sestra Miriam: **„Nisi problem koji treba popraviti, nego osoba koju treba ljubiti.”** Kad ju je prvi put čuo, pogodila ga je ravno u srce, jer se upravo tako odnosio prema supruzi. Dodaje i misao svetog Vinka Paulskog: **„Onaj tko žuri, odgađa Božje stvari.”**
sections.subtitle_en: An "Activator" who is often impatient: when strengths from ministry backfire on marriage
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest quotes Sister Miriam: "You are not a problem to be solved, but a person to be loved"
sections.content_en:
Monette honestly admits that patient presence is not his natural way of giving love. He likes to solve problems, take risks, and try new things. As confirmation, he cites the results of personality tests widespread in the USA. On the Strength Finders test, his strongest trait is **Activator**, with the description "is often impatient." On the Working Genius test, **Tenacity and Galvanizing** stand out. When the translator stumbled over those expressions, the guest asked for applause for him and "translated" them himself: "I want to get things moving and get you moving along with me. And if someone isn't ready to go, I simply go to those who are."

In ministry, he says, those are great traits. They are the mark of an evangelizer, one whom in his community they call a "harvester," and the Church needs such people. **In marriage, however, one cannot leave for someone else who is more ready.** The more he succeeded as a professional minister, the more he created an atmosphere in which his wife's **wounds of rejection and abandonment** deepened. The atmosphere of the home was shaped by everything he did outside of it, with the message "we move at a fast pace." Time with his wife often boiled down to diagnosing: how do we fix you and bring you up to our speed?

The guest then asks how many of those present were recently in Međugorje at a gathering of the John Paul II Healing Center, after which the name of Bob Schuchts is also mentioned. He cites a sentence frequently repeated by Sister Miriam: **"You are not a problem to be solved, but a person to be loved."** When he first heard it, it hit him straight in the heart, because that was exactly how he had been treating his wife. He also adds a thought from Saint Vincent de Paul: **"Whoever is in a hurry delays the things of God."**

sections.subtitle: Kriza nakon šest godina: „Kevine, samo se pojavi”
sections.screenshot_description: Kevin Monette opisuje kako je svake večeri bez mobitela i televizije sjedao na kauč i čekao
sections.content:
Nakon šest godina braka Monette i supruga zapali su u krizu i nisu znali kako je riješiti. Tada je, kaže, osjetio kako mu Duh Sveti govori: **„Kevine, samo se pojavi. Nemoj imati plan, nemoj imati ometanja, samo budi.”** Njegova prva reakcija bila je zbunjenost: kako se to radi?

Odgovor je postala jednostavna navika. Svake večeri, kad djeca odu spavati, sjedao je na kauč **bez mobitela, bez upaljenog televizora i bez ikakvih ometanja** i mirno čekao, „kao luđak”, dodaje uz smijeh. Ako mu se supruga htjela pridružiti, mogla je. Ako nije, ostao bi ondje i molio. Razgovarao je s Gospodinom, ali je pritom bio spreman da ga se u svakom trenutku prekine. „Kvalitetno vrijeme ne možeš isforsirati, ali se možeš postaviti tako da budeš spreman primiti ga”, objašnjava. Na taj način supružnika dočekujemo na njegovoj razini i u njegovom tempu.

Sliku dočarava **utrkom na tri noge**, u kojoj je jedna noga zajednička i svoj korak moraš uskladiti s drugim. Spominje i psihološka istraživanja takozvane **sinkronizacije srca**. Prema studiji sa Sveučilišta Princeton koju navodi, kad su ljudi emocionalno usklađeni i vode razgovor u kojem se izmjenjuju, njihovi se otkucaji srca **fizički sinkroniziraju**. Tada je **70 posto vjerojatnije da će zajednički donositi odluke**. „Znanstveno nam to pokazuje: želite li slogu u braku, morate uskladiti tempo i doći supružniku na njegovu razinu”, zaključuje gost. Onima u službi poručuje: ako je tempo supružnika sporiji od tempa službe, treba ili usporiti ili se povući.
sections.subtitle_en: Crisis after six years: "Kevin, just show up"
sections.screenshot_description_en: Kevin Monette describes how every evening without a phone or television he would sit on the couch and wait
sections.content_en:
After six years of marriage, Monette and his wife fell into a crisis and did not know how to resolve it. At that point, he says, he felt the Holy Spirit saying to him: **"Kevin, just show up. Have no agenda, have no distractions, just be."** His first reaction was confusion: how do you do that?

The answer became a simple habit. Every evening, when the children went to sleep, he sat on the couch **without a phone, without the television turned on, and without any distractions** and quietly waited, "like a crazy person," he adds with a laugh. If his wife wanted to join him, she could. If not, he would stay there and pray. He talked with the Lord, but was at the same time ready to be interrupted at any moment. "You cannot force quality time, but you can position yourself so that you are ready to receive it," he explains. In that way, we meet the spouse at their level and at their pace.

He illustrates the image with a **three-legged race**, in which one leg is shared and you must adjust your step to the other. He also mentions psychological research on so-called **heart rate synchronization**. According to a study from Princeton University that he cites, when people are emotionally attuned and engage in a conversation where they take turns, their heartbeats **physically synchronize**. Then they are **70 percent more likely to make decisions together**. "Science shows this to us: if you want harmony in marriage, you must match the pace and meet the spouse at their level," the guest concludes. To those in ministry, he says: if the spouse's pace is slower than the ministry's pace, one must either slow down or step back.

sections.subtitle: „Voliš službu više od mene”: ostavka koja je spasila odnos
sections.screenshot_description: Gost prepričava savjet duhovnika da napusti službu
sections.content:
Jedna rečenica njegove supruge, izgovorena dok je bila duboko povrijeđena, posebno je pogodila Monettea: **„Kevine, ti voliš službu više nego mene.”** Znao je da to nije istina. No to što ona tako vjeruje i to mu govori pokazalo mu je da su, kako kaže, „jako daleko od toga da budemo usklađeni”.

Kad je to iznio svom duhovniku, dobio je odgovor koji nije očekivao: „Kevine, mislim da moraš otpustiti službu.” Odluka nije bila laka. Godinama je gradio tim: svakog je tjedna dolazilo **stotine ljudi**, s njim je služilo **35 do 40 volontera**, a nitko nije bio spreman preuzeti vodstvo. Ipak je **već sljedećeg dana poslao e-mail s ostavkom**, iako, kako priznaje, nije znao hoće li se ikada vratiti služenju.

Upravo nakon tog e-maila počeo je dolaziti na kauč. Kad je supruzi rekao za ostavku, nije bila oduševljena, ali dogodilo se nešto suptilno: **nešto je u njoj omekšalo**. Kao da je otpao sloj laži da on voli službu više nego nju. U sljedećim mjesecima zajedničkog sjedenja na kauču doživjeli su, kaže, mnogo obnove.

Gost ne obećava da će svatko proći isti put kao on i supruga Rose, ali ističe da je takva odluka „potpuno vrijedna toga, jer Isus sve čini novo”. Na kraju dodaje iznenađenje: **Encounter Ministries preporučila mu je upravo supruga.** U toj je zajednici vidio više čudesa nego u više od deset godina prethodnog služenja zajedno. Ali sada je, naglašava, **ona bila s njim u tome**. „Ljubav je strpljiva”, zatvara on prvu cjelinu.
sections.subtitle_en: "You love ministry more than me": the resignation that saved the relationship
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest recounts the spiritual director's advice to leave ministry
sections.content_en:
One sentence from his wife, uttered while she was deeply hurt, struck Monette especially hard: **"Kevin, you love ministry more than me."** He knew that was not true. But the fact that she believed that and told him so showed him that they were, as he says, "very far from being aligned."

When he presented this to his spiritual director, he received an answer he did not expect: "Kevin, I think you need to let go of ministry." The decision was not easy. For years he had been building a team: every week **hundreds of people** came, **35 to 40 volunteers** served with him, and no one was ready to take over the leadership. Yet **the very next day he sent a resignation email**, even though, as he admits, he did not know whether he would ever return to ministry.

It was right after that email that he started coming to the couch. When he told his wife about the resignation, she was not thrilled, but something subtle happened: **something inside her softened**. It was as if a layer of the lie that he loved ministry more than her had fallen away. In the following months of sitting together on the couch, they experienced, he says, much renewal.

The guest does not promise that everyone will walk the same path as he and his wife Rose, but emphasizes that such a decision is "completely worth it, because Jesus makes all things new." At the end, he adds a surprise: **it was his wife who recommended Encounter Ministries to him.** In that community he saw more miracles than in more than ten years of previous ministry together. But now, he emphasizes, **she was with him in it**. "Love is patient," he closes the first part.

sections.subtitle: Dobrostivost i lekcija o ćelavom proroku
sections.screenshot_description: Kevin Monette prepričava zgodu iz Druge knjige o kraljevima o Elizeju i dječacima
sections.content:
Druga cjelina glasi **ljubav je dobrostiva i nije nepristojna**. Već na početku nastaje mali zaplet: prevoditelj najprije kaže „ljubav je nježna”, a onda ispravlja u „dobrostiva” i napominje da se prijevodi znatno razlikuju. „Vaš je vjerojatno točan”, odgovara gost uz smijeh. Publika zatim izgovara: **„Ja sam dobrostiv. Nisam nepristojan.”**

Kao „jedan od najupečatljivijih biblijskih odlomaka o nepristojnosti” Monette parafrazira drugo poglavlje Druge knjige o kraljevima. Prorok Elizej upravo je primio dvostruki dio Ilijina duha i odmah zatim na čudesan način pročistio vodu za cijeli grad. „Super, zar ne?”, pita gost, a kad publika ne reagira, dodaje: „Nikome to nije super.” Na putu prema Betelu iz grada izlaze dječaci i rugaju mu se: **„Odlazi, ćelavi! Odlazi, ćelavi!”** Prorok se okreće i proklinje ih u ime Gospodnje, a iz šume izlaze **dvije medvjedice i rastrgaju 42 dječaka**. „Riječ Gospodnja”, zaključuje gost.

Uz osmijeh dodaje da ne zna je li Elizej bio nesiguran zbog gubitka kose. Jasno mu je ipak jedno: **Gospodin ne voli nepristojnost prema onima koje ljubi.** Iz toga izvodi praktičnu pouku: možda bi nas ovaj odlomak trebao zaustaviti prije nego što kritiziramo kako supružnik izgleda.
sections.subtitle_en: Kindness and the lesson about the bald prophet
sections.screenshot_description_en: Kevin Monette recounts the incident from the Second Book of Kings about Elisha and the boys
sections.content_en:
The second section is **love is kind and is not rude**. Right at the beginning a small complication arises: the translator first says "love is gentle," and then corrects it to "kind" and notes that translations differ considerably. "Yours is probably accurate," the guest responds with a laugh. The audience then declares: **"I am kind. I am not rude."**

As "one of the most striking biblical passages about rudeness," Monette paraphrases the second chapter of the Second Book of Kings. The prophet Elisha had just received a double portion of Elijah's spirit and immediately after miraculously purified the water for the whole city. "Cool, right?", the guest asks, and when the audience does not react, he adds: "Nobody thinks that's cool." On the way to Bethel, boys come out of the city and jeer at him: **"Go away, baldy! Go away, baldy!"** The prophet turns around and curses them in the name of the Lord, and out of the woods come **two female bears and tear apart 42 boys**. "The word of the Lord," the guest concludes.

With a smile, he adds that he does not know if Elisha was insecure about his hair loss. One thing, however, is clear to him: **the Lord does not like rudeness toward those He loves.** From that he draws a practical lesson: perhaps this passage should give us pause before we criticize how our spouse looks.

sections.subtitle: Vidjeti supružnika Božjim očima, i usred svađe
sections.screenshot_description: Gost opisuje molitvu u tri koraka kojom traži da suprugu vidi onako kako je vidi Bog
sections.content:
Kad govori o dobrostivosti, Monette zapravo govori o **časti**: odnosim li se prema drugome s dostojanstvom koje mu je Bog dao? Posebno, naglašava, **usred neslaganja**, kada se blagovaonički stol čini poput stola koji je Gospodin postavio pred licem neprijatelja. U takvim trenucima zbog nečije slomljenosti često ne vidimo njegovo dostojanstvo, pa treba zatražiti Božju perspektivu.

Gost opisuje vlastitu molitvu u tri koraka:

1. **„Pomozi mi da svog supružnika najprije vidim kao Tvoje ljubljeno dijete.”**
2. **„Pomozi mi da ga vidim kako hoda u punoj sigurnosti Tvoje ljubavi.”**
3. **„Pomozi mi da ga vidim kako hoda u punini darova koje si stavio nad njegov život.”**

Kad god tako vidi suprugu onako kako je Bog vidi, bez obzira na to koliko mu se ona u tom trenutku činila nepristojnom ili ravnodušnom, „a takav sam i ja prema njoj, budimo fer”, dodaje, **ponovno se zaljubi u nju**.

Priznaje i da je ljudima govorio kako je proročki vidio da će njegova supruga, kad konačno bude hodala u punom autoritetu, imati više snage od njega. „I ja postanem ljubomoran”, kaže uz smijeh. Kad su o tome razgovarali, saznao je da ona isto čini za njega i ima istu viziju o njemu. „Vidjeti Očevu viziju o supružniku iznimno je snažno”, zaključuje Monette.
sections.subtitle_en: Seeing the spouse through God's eyes, even in the middle of a fight
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest describes a three-step prayer asking to see his wife the way God sees her
sections.content_en:
When speaking about kindness, Monette is actually speaking about **honor**: do I treat the other person with the dignity that God gave them? Especially, he emphasizes, **in the middle of a disagreement**, when the dining table feels like the table that the Lord prepared in the presence of enemies. In such moments, because of someone's brokenness, we often do not see their dignity, so one needs to ask for God's perspective.

The guest describes his own three-step prayer:

1. **"Help me to see my spouse first as Your beloved child."**
2. **"Help me to see them walking in the full security of Your love."**
3. **"Help me to see them walking in the fullness of the gifts You have placed over their life."**

Whenever he sees his wife the way God sees her like that, regardless of how rude or indifferent she might seem to him at that moment—"and I am that way toward her too, let's be fair," he adds—**he falls in love with her all over again**.

He also admits that he used to tell people how he prophetically saw that his wife, when she finally walks in full authority, will have more strength than him. "And I get jealous," he says with a laugh. When they talked about it, he found out that she does the same for him and has the same vision about him. "Seeing the Father's vision of the spouse is extremely powerful," Monette concludes.

sections.subtitle: Ljubav ne traži svoje: ispovijest jednog Amerikanca i najmlađeg djeteta
sections.screenshot_description: Kevin Monette govori o konferenciji dr. Boba Schutza i pohlepi kao navezanosti na sigurnost
sections.content:
Treća cjelina glasi **ljubav ne zavidi i ne traži svoje**. Nakon deklaracija „Ja ne zavidim” i „Ne tražim svoje” i trenutka tišine, Monette počinje šaljivom ispovijedi. „Ja sam Amerikanac, mi tražimo svoje”, kaže i navodi podatak da Amerikanci čine **4 posto svjetskog stanovništva, a troše trećinu svjetske potrošnje**.

Slijedi drugo priznanje: najmlađe je dijete u obitelji. „Mi smo malo zaokupljeni sobom”, kaže, a najstarijoj djeci u publici dobacuje da se ne moraju s tim „tako oduševljeno složiti”. Objašnjava i zašto: najmlađi se većinu vremena nisu morali ni za koga brinuti. „Nije naša krivnja što je mama prestala imati djecu.”

Ozbiljniji dio priče počinje 2019., kad je sa suprugom bio na konferenciji **„Healing the Whole Person”** (Iscjeljenje cijele osobe) dr. Boba Schutza. Dr. Bob uz **sedam glavnih grijeha** govori i o **sedam smrtnih rana**. Monette se iznenadio kad se prepoznao u **pohlepi**. Nikad nije mislio da je to njegov problem, jer je odrastao u obitelji bez mnogo novca. Ipak, pogodilo ga je kad je čuo da je **pohlepa zapravo navezanost na sigurnost**: umjesto da se oslonimo na Boga koji se brine za nas, oslanjamo se na stvari. Shvatio je da je gomilanje jeftinih stvari koje im nisu trebale, a koje je obitelj prakticirala, zapravo bilo grešno.
sections.subtitle_en: Love does not insist on its own way: confession of an American and the youngest child
sections.screenshot_description_en: Kevin Monette speaks about Dr. Bob Schuchts's conference and greed as attachment to security
sections.content_en:
The third section is **love does not envy and does not insist on its own way**. After the declarations "I do not envy" and "I do not insist on my own way" and a moment of silence, Monette begins with a humorous confession. "I am an American, we insist on our own way," he says, citing data that Americans make up **4 percent of the world's population, yet consume a third of the world's consumption**.

A second admission follows: he is the youngest child in the family. "We are a little self-absorbed," he says, calling out to the oldest children in the audience that they do not have to "agree so enthusiastically" with that. He also explains why: the youngest most of the time did not have to take care of anyone. "It's not our fault that Mom stopped having children."

The more serious part of the story begins in 2019, when he and his wife attended the conference **"Healing the Whole Person"** by Dr. Bob Schuchts. Dr. Bob, alongside the **seven deadly sins**, also speaks about the **seven deadly wounds**. Monette was surprised when he recognized himself in **greed**. He never thought that was his problem, because he grew up in a family without much money. Still, it struck him when he heard that **greed is actually an attachment to security**: instead of relying on God who cares for us, we rely on things. He realized that hoarding cheap things they did not need, which the family practiced, was actually sinful.

sections.subtitle: Kutija s osam pari cipela i dobrota koja vodi obraćenju
sections.screenshot_description: Gost opisuje kako je otvorio golemu kutiju s natpisom „Besplatni dar” i u njoj pronašao osam pari cipela
sections.content:
Uvjerenje o pohlepi, priča Monette, stiglo je nekoliko mjeseci kasnije, na neočekivan način. Na eBayu je pronašao par cipela svog broja za **9 dolara, s besplatnom dostavom**, „jeftinije od 9 eura”, dodaje za domaću publiku. Nakon narudžbe primijetio je da isti prodavač nudi još jedan par za 5 dolara i još dva para za po 1 dolar, sve s besplatnom dostavom. Bez pitanja supruge kupio je sve.

„Znam što mislite, ali niste u pravu: stigle su”, nastavlja. Pošiljka je došla u golemoj kutiji. Kad je skinuo traku, na vrhu je stajao natpis **„Free Gift”** (besplatni dar). Brojeći je pronašao **osam pari cipela**: uz četiri naručena, još četiri gratis. Dio njega bio je „poprilično uznemiren”, pa je očekivao da će se oglasiti glas: „Ovaj paket samouništit će se za 3, 2, 1.”

U tom se trenutku okrenuo Gospodinu: **„Gospodine, ne treba mi nijedan od ovih parova.”** Prisjetio se riječi svetog Pavla iz Poslanice Rimljanima da **Božja dobrota vodi k pokajanju**. Bio je toliko potresen da je **sve cipele poklonio**.

To ga je uvjerenje pratilo i dalje. Kad bi u trgovini naišao na dva jednaka proizvoda, jedan na sniženju, a drugi ne, kupio bi skuplji. Nije to činio zato što je bio bolji, nego zato što je želio **slomiti moć koju je pohlepa imala nad njim**. Time je, kaže, htio odgovoriti i na nešto što mu je Gospodin rekao godinama ranije.
sections.subtitle_en: A box with eight pairs of shoes and the goodness that leads to repentance
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest describes how he opened a huge box with the label "Free Gift" and found eight pairs of shoes inside
sections.content_en:
The conviction about greed, Monette relates, arrived a few months later, in an unexpected way. On eBay he found a pair of shoes in his size for **9 dollars, with free shipping**, "cheaper than 9 euros," he adds for the local audience. After ordering, he noticed that the same seller was offering another pair for 5 dollars and two more pairs for 1 dollar each, all with free shipping. Without asking his wife, he bought them all.

"I know what you're thinking, but you're wrong: they arrived," he continues. The shipment came in a huge box. When he removed the tape, on top was the inscription **"Free Gift"**. Counting them, he found **eight pairs of shoes**: alongside the four ordered, four more for free. A part of him was "quite disturbed," so he expected a voice to announce: "This package will self-destruct in 3, 2, 1."

At that moment he turned to the Lord: **"Lord, I don't need any of these pairs."** He recalled the words of Saint Paul from the Letter to the Romans that **God's kindness leads to repentance**. He was so shaken that he **gave away all the shoes**.

That conviction stayed with him further. Whenever in a store he encountered two identical products, one on sale and the other not, he would buy the more expensive one. He did not do that because he was better, but because he wanted to **break the power that greed had over him**. In doing so, he says, he also wanted to respond to something the Lord had told him years earlier.

sections.subtitle: Molitvena grupa, manifestacije i odgovor koji je glasio: nenavezanost
sections.screenshot_description: Kevin Monette prepričava kako je u autu vapio Bogu i čuo riječ „nenavezanost”
sections.content:
Riječ od prije mnogo godina vezana je uz razdoblje kad je upoznao suprugu, u **molitvenoj grupi mladih**. Većina toga što se ondje događalo bila je dobra i molili su jedni za druge. U maloj grupi od sedam ili osam ljudi primijetili su ipak nešto uznemirujuće. Kad bi molitva postala posebno pomazana, **otprilike polovica djevojaka, među njima i Rose**, završila bi na podu, grčeći se u nečemu što su prepoznali kao **demonske manifestacije**. Voditelji su pazili da sve bude sigurno, ali se u biti samo čekalo da prođe. Ništa se nije razrješavalo, a događalo se svaki tjedan.

Monette se sjeća kako je jednog dana, vozeći se kući, u suzama vapio: **„Gospodine, što je potrebno da naše sestre budu oslobođene?”** Odgovor, „jasan kao dan”, iznenadio ga je: **nenavezanost**. Iz njega je odmah izletjelo: **„Ne.”**

Bilo je to, kaže, kao da mu Bog govori: „Kevine, ako se želiš suprotstaviti neprijatelju, ne smiješ biti podijeljen. Iskoristit će to protiv tebe.” U tom je trenutku znao da je navezan na mnogo toga:

- **filmove**,
- **glazbu**,
- **kupovinu**,
- **alkohol**.

Nije bio spreman to otpustiti. Služio je **dvojici gospodara, Bogu i mamonu**, i s tim je ušao u brak.
sections.subtitle_en: Prayer group, manifestations, and the answer that was: detachment
sections.screenshot_description_en: Kevin Monette recounts how in the car he cried out to God and heard the word "detachment"
sections.content_en:
The word from years before is tied to the period when he met his wife, in a **youth prayer group**. Most of what took place there was good, and they prayed for one another. In a small group of seven or eight people, however, they noticed something disturbing. Whenever the prayer became especially anointed, **about half of the girls, among them Rose**, would end up on the floor, writhing in what they recognized as **demonic manifestations**. The leaders made sure everything was safe, but basically everyone just waited for it to pass. Nothing was resolved, and it happened every week.

Monette remembers how one day, driving home, he cried out in tears: **"Lord, what is needed for our sisters to be delivered?"** The answer, "clear as day," surprised him: **detachment**. Straight out of him came: **"No."**

It was, he says, as if God was telling him: "Kevin, if you want to stand against the enemy, you cannot be divided. He will use it against you." At that moment he knew that he was attached to many things:

- **movies**,
- **music**,
- **shopping**,
- **alcohol**.

He was not ready to let that go. He was serving **two masters, God and mammon**, and with that he entered into marriage.

sections.subtitle: Stotine filmova i rečenica: „Što zadržiš, pustit će korijenje u tvom domu”
sections.screenshot_description: Gost prenosi riječ koju je primio: „Kevine, što zadržiš, pustit će korijenje u tvom domu”
sections.content:
Monette posebno govori o zabavi. Odrastao je u vrlo zaštićenom domu u kojem se nije gledalo mnogo filmova. Kao odrastao čovjek mogao je gledati što god želi. U zalagaonici su DVD-i stajali po 2 dolara, pa je skupio **zbirku od stotina filmova** i jednako golemu zbirku glazbe, i sve je bilo **svjetovno**. „Koliko je od tog okruženja, svih tih glasova i sadržaja, bilo sveto?”, pita publiku.

Primijetio je obrazac: kad bi pustio nešto mračnije, ta bi se tama **zadržavala u domu**, prije svega kod supruge. Gotovo svaki put imala bi **noćne more ili noćne napadaje straha** i ljutila se na njega što ju je nagovorio da s njim gleda.

Kad je počeo ulaziti u službu iscjeljenja, osjetio je kako mu Gospodin govori: **„Kevine, što zadržiš, pustit će korijenje u tvom domu.”** Jednog je dana uzeo u ruke svaki od stotina filmova i postavio dva pitanja:

1. **Ostavlja li me ovo izgrađenim, ohrabrenim i utješenim?** Ako je odgovor bio ne, film je išao na hrpu za bacanje.
2. **Utječe li ovo negativno na moju suprugu?** Ako je odgovor bio da, i taj je završio na istoj hrpi.

Neke je filmove iskreno volio, ali osjetio je kako ga Bog uči: **„Kevine, sada si jedno. Što je prepreka tvom supružniku, prepreka je i tebi.”** To vrijedi čak i kad sam nema nikakav problem s tim sadržajem, jer **ljubav ne traži svoje**, nego jedinstvo i kompatibilnost. Gost pritom ističe da latinsko podrijetlo riječi „kompatibilan” znači **„trpjeti s nekim”**. Na neki način križevi supružnika postaju naši. Zato poručuje: ako nešto supružnika vodi u grijeh, treba to odrezati.
sections.subtitle_en: Hundreds of movies and the sentence: "What you keep will take root in your home"
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest conveys the word he received: "Kevin, what you keep will take root in your home"
sections.content_en:
Monette speaks specifically about entertainment. He grew up in a very sheltered home where they did not watch many movies. As an adult, he was able to watch whatever he wanted. At the pawnshop DVDs cost 2 dollars each, so he gathered a **collection of hundreds of movies** and an equally huge collection of music, and it was all **secular**. "How much of that environment, all those voices and content, was holy?", he asks the audience.

He noticed a pattern: whenever he played something darker, that darkness would **linger in the home**, first of all with his wife. Almost every time she would have **nightmares or night terrors** and get angry with him for persuading her to watch with him.

When he began entering into the healing ministry, he felt the Lord saying to him: **"Kevin, what you keep will take root in your home."** One day he took into his hands each of the hundreds of movies and asked two questions:

1. **Does this leave me built up, encouraged, and comforted?** If the answer was no, the movie went onto the discard pile.
2. **Does this negatively affect my wife?** If the answer was yes, that one ended up on the same pile too.

Some of the movies he genuinely loved, but he felt God teaching him: **"Kevin, now you are one. What is a stumbling block to your spouse is a stumbling block to you."** That holds true even when he himself has no problem with that content, because **love does not insist on its own way**, but seeks unity and compatibility. The guest emphasizes in this regard that the Latin origin of the word "compatible" means **"to suffer with someone"**. In a way, the spouse's crosses become ours. That is why he says: if something leads the spouse into sin, it should be cut off.

sections.subtitle: Glazba koja nosi duh, bez osude, i plodovi promjene
sections.screenshot_description: Kevin Monette govori o četrdesetak knjiga o iscjeljenju koje je sa suprugom pročitao u jednoj godini
sections.content:
Monette ukratko govori i o glazbi. Glazba slavljenja, primjećuje, pomaže uvesti dušu u Božju prisutnost i na neki je način duhovno prožeta molitvom autora. Pita publiku je li ikada pomislila da je i **svjetovna glazba duhovno prožeta**. Sam je svirao u rock bendovima, a ono što je najviše slušao bilo je ispunjeno slomljenim srcima, egom i bijesom, jer su autori tako ispuštali svoju bol. „I ja to dovodim u naš dom i zajedno to pjevamo”, kaže.

Čita iz Poslanice Efežanima 4: iz usta ne smije izlaziti nikakva ružna riječ, nego samo ona koja je dobra za izgradnju. Svaka gorčina, srdžba, gnjev, vika i psovka moraju se ukloniti. Priznaje da je na sve to bio jako navezan. Isti tekst nastavlja: **„Ne dajte mjesta đavlu.”** Bio je duboko uvjeren i **riješio se svega**.

Potom moli publiku da ga pažljivo sasluša: ovo ne dijeli kako bi ikoga osudio zbog onoga što gleda ili sluša, niti kako bi raspravljao što je umjetnost ili što je prihvatljivo prema katoličkom nauku. Prepreke svakog bračnog para drukčije su od njegovih. Želi ipak da se čuje **plod** tih promjena:

- **ozračje doma malo se po malo promijenilo**, a bez vanjskih glasova odjednom je postalo vrlo lako moliti,
- počeo je učiti svirati gitaru, iako je kod kuće imao pet gitara koje nikad nije naučio svirati, i to pjesme slavljenja, „jer trebaju samo četiri akorda”,
- obitelj je počela **zajedno slaviti Boga**,
- dok su sjedali na kauč, on i Rose počeli su zajedno čitati duhovnu literaturu: on bi čitao naglas, a zatim bi zastali i vodili duboke razgovore.

U samo jednoj godini pročitali su **više od 40 knjiga o iscjeljenju i oslobođenju**. Za Monettea je to velika stvar, jer u prethodnih deset godina nije dovršio nijednu knjigu. „Ljubav ne zavidi, ne traži svoje”, zaključuje treću cjelinu i najavljuje sljedeću.
sections.subtitle_en: Music that carries a spirit, without judgment, and the fruits of change
sections.screenshot_description_en: Kevin Monette speaks about roughly forty books on healing that he read with his wife in a single year
sections.content_en:
Monette also speaks briefly about music. Worship music, he observes, helps usher the soul into God's presence and is in a way spiritually imbued with the prayer of the author. He asks the audience if they have ever thought that **secular music is also spiritually imbued**. He himself played in rock bands, and what he listened to most was filled with broken hearts, ego, and rage, because the authors were venting their pain that way. "And I bring that into our home and we sing it together," he says.

He reads from Ephesians 4: no foul language should come out of your mouth, but only what is good for building up. All bitterness, fury, anger, shouting, and reviling must be removed. He admits that he was very attached to all of that. The same text continues: **"Do not give room to the devil."** He was deeply convicted and **got rid of everything**.

Then he asks the audience to listen to him carefully: he is not sharing this in order to condemn anyone for what they watch or listen to, nor to debate what is art or what is acceptable according to Catholic teaching. Every married couple's obstacles are different from his. He wants, however, for the **fruit** of those changes to be heard:

- **the atmosphere of the home changed little by little**, and without outside voices it suddenly became very easy to pray,
- he started learning to play the guitar, even though he had five guitars at home that he never learned to play, specifically worship songs, "because they only take four chords",
- the family began to **worship God together**,
- as they sat on the couch, he and Rose began reading spiritual literature together: he would read aloud, and then they would pause and have deep conversations.

In just one year they read **more than 40 books on healing and deliverance**. For Monette, that is a big deal, because in the previous ten years he had not finished a single book. "Love does not envy, does not insist on its own way," he concludes the third section and announces the next.

iterations.theme_en: Keys of love from 1 Cor 13: patience, kindness, and detachment (love does not insist on its own way)
