sections.subtitle: „Ljubav se ne nadima“: od deklaracije do najranjivijeg dijela večeri
sections.screenshot_description: Kevin Monette najavljuje da će s publikom podijeliti najranjiviji dio svoje priče
sections.content:
Kevin Monette nastavlja prolaziti kroz Pavlov himan ljubavi iz Prve poslanice Korinćanima i dolazi do retka **„Ljubav se ne nadima, ne hvasta se“**. Kao i kod prethodnih atributa, poziva okupljene da ga izgovore nad sobom: **„Ne nadimam se. Ne hvastam se.“** Zatim ih potiče da osluhnu kako ta rečenica zvuči kad izađe iz njihovih usta.

Nakon kratke tišine najavljuje da želi biti ranjiv i pita publiku je li to u redu. Uz osmijeh dodaje da je u tjednu provedenom u Hrvatskoj shvatio kako to „nije baš hrvatski način“.

Podsjeća da je i nakon vjenčanja nastavio voditi službu. U prvih pet godina braka on i supruga dobili su **troje djece**, a on je i dalje vodio. Iskreno priznaje i razlog: na mnoge je načine osjećao da mora izaći iz kuće kako bi iskusio Kristovu ljubav. Voditi duhovne obnove i gledati kako ljudi dolaze Isusu bilo je, kaže, iznimno uzbudljivo.

Kod kuće je slika bila drukčija. Kad bi se vratio, osjećao je **tamu i kaos**. Supruga je bila preplavljena, i to ne samo brigom o djeci. Oko šeste godine braka na površinu su počeli izlaziti dijelovi njezine prošlosti. Oni su, kako Monette objašnjava, počeli oblikovati ono što je ona vjerovala o njemu i o njihovu braku.
sections.subtitle_en: "Love is not pompous": from declaration to the most vulnerable part of the evening
sections.screenshot_description_en: Kevin Monette announces that he will share the most vulnerable part of his story with the audience
sections.content_en:
Kevin Monette continues going through Paul's hymn of love from the First Letter to the Corinthians and arrives at the verse **"Love is not pompous, it is not boastful"**. As with previous attributes, he invites those gathered to declare it over themselves: **"I am not pompous. I do not boast."** Then he encourages them to listen to how that sentence sounds when it leaves their mouth.

After a brief silence, he announces that he wants to be vulnerable and asks the audience if that is okay. With a smile, he adds that during the week spent in Croatia he realized that this is "not really the Croatian way."

He recalls that even after the wedding he continued leading ministry. In the first five years of marriage, he and his wife had **three children**, and he still continued leading. He honestly admits the reason as well: in many ways he felt that he had to leave the house in order to experience Christ's love. Leading retreats and watching people come to Jesus was, he says, extremely exciting.

At home, the picture was different. When he returned, he felt **darkness and chaos**. His wife was overwhelmed, and not just with caring for the children. Around the sixth year of marriage, parts of her past began coming to the surface. They began, as Monette explains, to shape what she believed about him and about their marriage.

sections.subtitle: Dan očeva i rečenica koja je slomila oca: „Volio bih da je tata mrtav“
sections.screenshot_description: Gost prepričava trenutak kad je čuo riječi svog petogodišnjeg djeteta
sections.content:
Najbolniji trenutak svoje priče Kevin Monette smješta na **Dan očeva**. Ulazio je u obiteljski kombi kad je čuo kako njegovo najstarije dijete, tada petogodišnji sin, govori majci: **„Volio bih da je tata mrtav. Želim novog tatu.“**

Ubrzo nakon toga supruga mu je priznala što je sinu odgovorila: da je to u redu i da mu Bog možda daje novog tatu. Uslijedili su, kako kaže, vrlo bolni razgovori.

Monette prepričava logiku koju je tada čuo od supruge:

- „Kevine, očajna sam u braku s tobom.“
- Ako mora ostati u braku, onda je Bog želi nesretnu.
- Ako je pak Bog ne želi nesretnu, onda za nju ima nekoga drugoga.

Budući da su vjerni katolici, to bi značilo da njihov brak nije valjan i da bi mogao biti **poništen**. Supruga je tome dodala i „svijetlu stranu“: tada bi se on mogao potpuno posvetiti službi, a možda bi čak mogao postati i svećenik.

Monette priznaje da je to bio **najveći udarac u trbuh koji je ikada doživio**. Opisuje kako je te riječi pratila gusta, podrugljiva tama. Znao je da ne dolaze samo od njegove žene i da utječu na njihovu djecu. Pokušao je razgovarati i urazumiti je, ali kaže da je to bilo kao da razgovara sa zidom.
sections.subtitle_en: Father's Day and the sentence that broke a father: "I wish Daddy was dead"
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest recounts the moment when he heard the words of his five-year-old child
sections.content_en:
Kevin Monette places the most painful moment of his story on **Father's Day**. He was getting into the family van when he heard his oldest child, then a five-year-old son, say to his mother: **"I wish Daddy was dead. I want a new daddy."**

Shortly after that, his wife admitted to him what she answered the son: that it was okay and that God might be giving him a new daddy. Very painful conversations followed, as he says.

Monette recounts the logic he heard from his wife at the time:

- "Kevin, I am miserable in marriage with you."
- If she has to stay in the marriage, then God wants her unhappy.
- If, on the other hand, God does not want her unhappy, then He has someone else for her.

Since they are faithful Catholics, that would mean that their marriage was not valid and that it could be **annulled**. His wife added a "bright side" to that: then he could dedicate himself entirely to ministry, and maybe he could even become a priest.

Monette admits that this was **the biggest gut punch he had ever experienced**. He describes how those words were accompanied by a thick, mocking darkness. He knew they did not come only from his wife and that they were affecting their children. He tried to talk and reason with her, but he says it was like talking to a brick wall.

sections.subtitle: Tjedan bez sna, molitva na koljenima i homilija: „Isus te neće rastaviti“
sections.screenshot_description: Kevin Monette opisuje noćnu molitvu na koljenima i jutarnju misu
sections.content:
Sljedećih tjedan dana Kevin Monette gotovo nije jeo ni spavao. Molio je, kaže, kao nikada prije, iz čistog očaja. Jedne večeri, na koljenima, izgovorio je: **„Gospodine, molim te. Ne znam kako je došlo do ovoga. Ali ako možeš spasiti moj brak, dat ću ti sve.“**

Jer nije mogao spavati, sljedećeg se jutra odvezao na vrlo ranu misu. Evanđelje toga dana bilo je **Isusovo učenje o rastavi**. Svećenik je u homiliji neprestano ponavljao: **„Isus te neće rastaviti. Isus te neće rastaviti.“** Monette je išao na pričest dok su mu suze lile niz lice. Sjeća se i pomisli da ga svećenik vjerojatno smatra vrlo čudnim.

U tom je razdoblju očajnički trebao prijatelja. Istodobno se bojao išta loše reći o svojoj supruzi. Isti ga strah, priznaje, čini da mu je i danas teško govoriti o tome. Ipak, ističe da je supruga s njim na putovanju i da je **„nevjerojatna žena, i uvijek je bila“**.

Objašnjava zašto ipak dijeli tako intimnu priču: **„Ponekad treba vidjeti dolinu da bi se razumjela pobjeda.“**
sections.subtitle_en: A week without sleep, prayer on knees, and a homily: "Jesus will not divorce you"
sections.screenshot_description_en: Kevin Monette describes nighttime prayer on his knees and morning Mass
sections.content_en:
For the next week, Kevin Monette hardly ate or slept. He prayed, he says, like never before, out of sheer desperation. One evening, on his knees, he spoke: **"Lord, please. I don't know how it came to this. But if you can save my marriage, I will give you everything."**

Because he could not sleep, the next morning he drove to a very early Mass. The Gospel of that day was **Jesus' teaching on divorce**. The priest in the homily repeatedly said: **"Jesus will not divorce you. Jesus will not divorce you."** Monette went to Communion while tears streamed down his face. He also remembers the thought that the priest probably considered him very strange.

During that period he desperately needed a friend. At the same time, he was afraid to say anything bad about his wife. The same fear, he admits, makes it difficult for him to speak about it even today. Yet, he emphasizes that his wife is with him on the journey and that she is **"an incredible woman, and always has been"**.

He explains why he shares such an intimate story anyway: **"Sometimes you have to see the valley to understand the victory."**

sections.subtitle: Psalam 34, poziv prijatelju i devetnica Gospi koja razvezuje čvorove
sections.screenshot_description: Gost govori o devetnici Gospi koja razvezuje čvorove i upozorava publiku uz osmijeh
sections.content:
Kevin Monette citira **Psalam 34**: „Gospodin je blizu onima slomljena srca i spašava one koji su klonuli duhom.“ Uz to je shvatio da kroz krizu ne može proći sam.

Nervozno je nazvao prijatelja koji je njega i suprugu svojedobno upoznao. Prijatelj ga je saslušao i, kako Monette kaže, *udahnuo mu život*. Pozvao ga je da izmoli **devetnicu Gospi koja razvezuje čvorove**. Publici Monette uz osmijeh dobacuje: „Ako je niste molili, pazite se.“

Prijatelj ga je savjetovao da supruzi pristupi s dvjema molbama:

- da mu se pridruži u devetnici, ali tako da je moli **sama, samostalno**;
- da dogovori **razgovor sa svećenikom** o stanju njihova braka.

S obzirom na to gdje su se tada nalazili, iznenadilo ga je što je pristala na oboje.

Do tada, priznaje, nije vidio mnogo čudesa. No tijekom **sljedećih devet dana** stvari su se počele mijenjati. Suprugina najbolja prijateljica javila joj se i počela je izazivati da potraži istinu o njihovu braku.

Budući da do supruge nije mogao doprijeti, Monette je okrenuo pogled prema sebi. Odlučio je potražiti ima li u njemu samome nešto što treba ozdravljenje.
sections.subtitle_en: Psalm 34, a call to a friend, and a novena to Our Lady, Undoer of Knots
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest speaks about the novena to Our Lady, Undoer of Knots, and warns the audience with a smile
sections.content_en:
Kevin Monette quotes **Psalm 34**: "The Lord is close to the brokenhearted and saves those who are crushed in spirit." Along with that, he realized that he could not go through the crisis alone.

He nervously called the friend who had originally introduced him and his wife. The friend listened to him and, as Monette says, *breathed life into him*. He invited him to pray the **novena to Our Lady, Undoer of Knots**. To the audience, Monette adds with a smile: "If you haven't prayed it, watch out."

The friend advised him to approach his wife with two requests:

- to join him in the novena, but in such a way that she prays it **alone, independently**;
- to arrange **a conversation with a priest** about the state of their marriage.

Given where they were at that time, it surprised him that she agreed to both.

Until then, he admits, he had not seen many miracles. But over **the next nine days**, things began to change. His wife's best friend reached out to her and began challenging her to seek the truth about their marriage.

Since he could not reach his wife, Monette turned his gaze inward. He decided to look whether there was something in himself that needed healing.

sections.subtitle: Stotine imena na papiru: molitva za raskidanje duševnih veza
sections.screenshot_description: Kevin Monette objašnjava pojam duševnih veza i priznaje vlastitu prošlost
sections.content:
U potrazi za vlastitim ozdravljenjem Kevin Monette naišao je na **molitvu za raskidanje duševnih veza**. Pojašnjava da su duševne veze *neuredne privrženosti* koje stvaramo s drugima. Kad nekome damo srce, dajemo mu i autoritet nad sobom i postajemo vezani uz njega. Jedan od najčešćih načina na koji takve veze nastaju jest **spolni odnos izvan braka**.

Otvoreno priznaje da je imao prošlost u kojoj je *ljubav tražio na svim krivim mjestima*. Njegove su veze vrlo brzo postajale fizičke, uz mnogo grijeha i srama. Kad nije bio u vezi, okretao se internetu i ondje konzumirao sadržaj.

Osjetio je da ga Gospodin poziva da zapiše svako ime. Ne samo osobe s kojima je bio fizički intiman, nego i sve za kojima je ikada požudno žudio. **„Imao sam stotine i stotine zapisanih imena. Nisam ponosan na to“**, priznaje. Osjećao je da im to duguje: gdje ih je nekoć koristio i objektivizirao za vlastiti užitak, sada je molitvom trebao vratiti dostojanstvo i njima i sebi.

Kao primjer navodi poznatu osobu i ponavlja riječi molitve:

> „U ime Isusovo opraštam toj poznatoj osobi što je svoje tijelo predstavljala na seksualan način. Opraštam vlasnicima mrežne stranice koji su to promovirali. U ime Isusovo raskidam svoju duševnu vezu s tom osobom. Vraćam autoritet koji sam joj dao time što sam za njom požudno žudio i uzimam natrag sve što mi je uzela. Perem našu povijest u krvi Isusovoj. Oče, molim te da je danas blagosloviš, povedeš prema svakom pokajanju koje joj je potrebno i dovedeš u odnos s tobom.“

To je ponovio za svaku osobu na popisu. Bio je to, kaže, *jako dug dan*. I danas, kad mu netko novi padne na pamet, istu molitvu izmoli i za tu osobu.
sections.subtitle_en: Hundreds of names on paper: prayer for breaking soul ties
sections.screenshot_description_en: Kevin Monette explains the concept of soul ties and admits his own past
sections.content_en:
In search of his own healing, Kevin Monette came across a **prayer for breaking soul ties**. He explains that soul ties are *disordered attachments* that we create with others. When we give someone our heart, we also give them authority over ourselves and become tied to them. One of the most common ways such ties are formed is **sexual relations outside of marriage**.

He openly admits that he had a past in which he *looked for love in all the wrong places*. His relationships very quickly became physical, with a lot of sin and shame. When he was not in a relationship, he turned to the internet and consumed content there.

He felt the Lord calling him to write down every name. Not only the persons with whom he was physically intimate, but also all those whom he had ever lustfully desired. **"I had hundreds and hundreds of names written down. I am not proud of that"**, he admits. He felt that he owed it to them: where he once used and objectified them for his own pleasure, now in prayer he needed to restore dignity both to them and to himself.

As an example, he mentions a famous person and repeats the words of the prayer:

> "In the name of Jesus, I forgive that celebrity for presenting her body in a sexual way. I forgive the website owners who promoted it. In the name of Jesus, I break my soul tie with that person. I take back the authority that I gave her by lusting after her, and I take back everything she took from me. I wash our history in the blood of Jesus. Father, I ask that You bless her today, lead her to whatever repentance she needs, and bring her into relationship with You."

He repeated that for every person on the list. It was, he says, *a very long day*. Even today, when someone new comes to mind, he prays the same prayer for that person as well.

sections.subtitle: Kad se slomi moć napasti: „Ja sam zauzet“
sections.screenshot_description: Gost svjedoči da je nakon molitve slomljena moć napasti nad njim
sections.content:
Kevin Monette zatim ističe što je smatra najvažnijim u ovom dijelu svjedočanstva. Snaga koju su napasti imale nad njim bila je tolika da se, kako slikovito kaže, *grčevito držao* kako bi sačuvao čistoću. Kad je završio molitvu, **ta se moć slomila i više je nije osjetio**.

**„To je milost“**, kaže, a dvorana na trenutak utihne.

Pritom želi biti posve jasan: napasti i dalje dolaze, jer su „prekrasne žene posvuda“. No sada su toliko očite da ih može jednostavno pogledati i reći: *„Ne, odlazi. Nije vrijedno toga. Ja sam zauzet.“* Dodaje da to tada nije shvaćao, ali da sada shvaća.
sections.subtitle_en: When the power of temptation is broken: "I am taken"
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest testifies that after the prayer the power of temptation over him was broken
sections.content_en:
Kevin Monette then points out what he considers most important in this part of the testimony. The power that temptations had over him was so great that, as he vividly puts it, he was *white-knuckling it* to keep his purity. When he finished the prayer, **that power was broken and he no longer felt it**.

**"That is grace"**, he says, and the hall falls silent for a moment.

In doing so, he wants to be completely clear: temptations still come, because "beautiful women are everywhere." But now they are so obvious that he can simply look at them and say: *"No, go away. It's not worth it. I am taken."* He adds that he did not understand that back then, but that he understands it now.

sections.subtitle: Transparentnost pred Rose i Očeva riječ: „Bol tvoje žene ima malo veze s tobom“
sections.screenshot_description: Kevin Monette prepričava trenutak kad je osjetio Božji glas usred vlastitog sloma
sections.content:
Nakon molitve Kevin Monette otišao je svojoj supruzi **Rose**. Rekao joj je da od nje ništa ne očekuje, ali da pred njom želi biti potpuno transparentan. Pokajao se što je nije stavljao na prvo mjesto i što nije bio osjetljiv za njezine potrebe. Podijelio je s njom i stvari koje je već ispovjedio i za koje je primio odrješenje, ali koje joj nikada nije rekao.

Rose ga je pogledala i odgovorila: **„Hvala ti što si to podijelio. Ali to ne mijenja kako se osjećam.“**

Iako zvuči čudno, Monette kaže da mu je u tom trenutku laknulo. Znao je da više nema ništa što bi mogao predati i da može prestati sam sebe izjedati. *„Ležao sam licem na zemlji. Dublju rupu više nisam mogao iskopati.“*

Tada je, kako svjedoči, **Bog Otac progovorio**: **„Kevine, bol tvoje žene ima vrlo malo veze s tobom.“**

Ta ga je riječ iznutra preusmjerila. Njegova molitva više nije bila samo vapaj da Bog spasi njegov brak. Počeo je moliti za suprugu: *„Gospodine, želim njezino ozdravljenje. Ono kroz što prolazi, želim da bude potpuno obnovljeno.“* Tada su ga, opisuje, počeli preplavljivati **valovi Božje utjehe**.
sections.subtitle_en: Transparency before Rose and the Father's word: "Your wife's pain has little to do with you"
sections.screenshot_description_en: Kevin Monette recounts the moment he sensed God's voice in the midst of his own breakdown
sections.content_en:
After the prayer, Kevin Monette went to his wife **Rose**. He told her that he expected nothing from her, but that he wanted to be completely transparent before her. He repented for not putting her first and for not being sensitive to her needs. He also shared with her things he had already confessed and for which he had received absolution, but which he had never told her.

Rose looked at him and answered: **"Thank you for sharing that. But that doesn't change how I feel."**

Even though it sounds strange, Monette says that at that moment he felt relieved. He knew that he had nothing left that he could surrender and that he could stop tearing himself apart. *"I was lying face down on the ground. I couldn't dig a deeper hole anymore."*

Then, as he testifies, **God the Father spoke**: **"Kevin, your wife's pain has very little to do with you."**

That word redirected him from within. His prayer was no longer just a cry for God to save his marriage. He began to pray for his wife: *"Lord, I want her healing. Whatever she is going through, I want it to be fully restored."* Then, he describes, **waves of God's comfort** began to wash over him.

sections.subtitle: Rosina isprika, razotkrivena laž i najlakše oproštenje
sections.screenshot_description: Gost opisuje trenutak kad mu se supruga došla ispričati
sections.content:
Nekoliko dana kasnije Rose je došla Kevinu Monetteu i ispričala mu se. Ispričala se što je dopustila da joj srce odluta i što se zatvorila za mogućnost da je Gospodin ozdravi **upravo unutar njihova braka**.

Ponizno mu je ispričala da je otišla pred Gospodina u molitvi i da je On **razotkrio laž**. Priznala je Bogu svoju nadu da bi joj odlazak od Kevina pomogao izliječiti srce. Gospodin joj je, prema njezinim riječima, odgovorio: **„Ne.“**

Monette se sjeća izraza njezina lica dok je to govorila. Na njemu je vidio bespomoćnost, kao da je tek tada shvatila da je bila obmanuta. Bio je šokiran riječima koje su izlazile iz njezinih usta, ali je u njima prepoznao *vapaj za pomoć*.

**„Nikad mi nije bilo tako lako nekome oprostiti“**, kaže. Znao je da je spreman učiniti sve što može kako bi joj pomogao da kroz to prođe. Ovu cjelinu zaključuje retkom od kojeg je krenuo: *„Ljubav se ne nadima, ne hvasta se.“*
sections.subtitle_en: Rose's apology, the lie exposed, and the easiest forgiveness
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest describes the moment his wife came to apologize to him
sections.content_en:
A few days later Rose came to Kevin Monette and apologized to him. She apologized for letting her heart wander and for closing herself off to the possibility of the Lord healing her **right within their marriage**.

She humbly told him that she had gone before the Lord in prayer and that He had **exposed the lie**. She admitted to God her hope that leaving Kevin would help heal her heart. The Lord, according to her words, replied: **"No."**

Monette remembers the look on her face as she spoke that. On it he saw helplessness, as if only then had she realized that she had been deceived. He was shocked by the words coming out of her mouth, but in them he recognized *a cry for help*.

**"It was never so easy for me to forgive someone"**, he says. He knew he was ready to do everything he could to help her get through it. He concludes this section with the verse from which he started: *"Love is not pompous, it is not boastful."*

sections.subtitle: Sveti Franjo Saleški i pitanje koje je sve promijenilo: odakle dolazi bol?
sections.screenshot_description: Kevin Monette citira svetog Franju Saleškog o braku kao vježbi mrtvljenja
sections.content:
Kevin Monette ubrzano prelazi na sljedeću skupinu atributa: **ljubav nije nagla, ne pamti zlo, ne raduje se nepravdi, a raduje se istini**. Prevoditelj s publikom izgovara deklaraciju: *„Ne pamtim zlo, ne radujem se nepravdi, radujem se istini.“*

Zatim citira **svetog Franju Saleškog**, koji je brak nazvao *„neprestanom vježbom u mrtvljenju“*. Monette tumači da u braku svakoga dana postajemo sve svetiji.

Kad su on i Rose primili milost da prestanu prebacivati krivnju jedno na drugo, počeli su postavljati drukčije pitanje: **odakle onda dolazi ova bol?** Podsjeća da su od samog početka braka imali neispunjena očekivanja u intimnosti. Jednoga dana rekao je Rose da, prema njegovu skromnom poznavanju psihologije i ozdravljenja, uzrok može biti jedan od dvaju:

- **zlostavljanje u prošlosti**, ili
- **otvorena vrata zlu u obitelji**, primjerice uključenost u okultno.

Rose se s tom procjenom složila. Zanimljivo je, ističe Monette, da se dijelova svoje prošlosti uopće nije mogla sjetiti.
sections.subtitle_en: Saint Francis de Sales and the Question That Changed Everything: Where Does the Pain Come From?
sections.screenshot_description_en: Kevin Monette quotes Saint Francis de Sales on marriage as an exercise in mortification
sections.content_en:
Kevin Monette quickly moves to the next group of attributes: **love is not irritable, keeps no record of wrongs, does not rejoice in injustice, but rejoices in truth**. The translator and the audience speak the declaration: *„I keep no record of wrongs, I do not rejoice in injustice, I rejoice in truth.“*

Then he quotes **Saint Francis de Sales**, who called marriage a *„continual exercise in mortification“*. Monette explains that in marriage every day we become ever more holy.

When he and Rose received the grace to stop shifting blame onto each other, they began to ask a different question: **where then does this pain come from?** He recalls that from the very beginning of their marriage they had unfulfilled expectations in intimacy. One day he told Rose that, according to his modest knowledge of psychology and healing, the cause could be one of two things:

- **abuse in the past**, or
- **an open door to evil in the family**, for example involvement in the occult.

Rose agreed with that assessment. Interestingly, Monette points out, she could not remember parts of her past at all.

sections.subtitle: Obiteljska tajna: sotonistički rituali i zlostavljanje u ranom djetinjstvu
sections.screenshot_description: Gost govori o tome što su potvrdili stariji članovi suprugine obitelji
sections.content:
Još istoga dana Kevin Monette i Rose pozvali su k sebi nekoliko starijih članova njezine obitelji kojima su vjerovali. Oni su potvrdili da su se u njihovu obiteljskom domu doista održavali **sotonistički rituali**. Potvrdili su i da je Rose kao vrlo malo dijete bila **zlostavljana**. Pojedinosti se, međutim, nisu mogli sjetiti.

Monette slikovito opisuje bespomoćnost koja je uslijedila: *„Kažemo: ‘Super, hvala.’ Oni odu. A mi se pitamo: što ćemo sad s tim?“*

Nekoliko minuta kasnije pala mu je na pamet jednostavna misao: da na internetu potraži *katoličku konferenciju za ozdravljenje*.
sections.subtitle_en: A Family Secret: Satanic Rituals and Early Childhood Abuse
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest speaks about what older members of his wife's family confirmed
sections.content_en:
That very same day, Kevin Monette and Rose invited over several older members of her family whom they trusted. They confirmed that **satanic rituals** had indeed taken place in their family home. They also confirmed that Rose had been **abused** as a very small child. Details, however, they could not recall.

Monette vividly describes the helplessness that followed: *„We say: ‘Great, thank you.’ They leave. And we wonder: what do we do with this now?“*

A few minutes later, a simple thought occurred to him: to search online for a *Catholic healing conference*.

sections.subtitle: Konferencija „Ozdravljenje cijele osobe“ i čudesno ozdravljenje od celijakije
sections.screenshot_description: Kevin Monette opisuje molitvu za fizičko ozdravljenje svoje supruge
sections.content:
Pretraga ih je odvela do **dr. Boba Schutza**. Konferencija se održavala dva tjedna kasnije, dva sata vožnje sjeverno od njihova doma, i na njoj je još bilo mjesta. Isplanirali su put i otišli.

Drugoga dana na konferenciji molilo se za **fizičko ozdravljenje**. Oko Rose se okupila skupina žena. Jedna od njih osjetila je snažnu bol u trbuhu i pomislila da bi to mogla biti bol koju dijeli s Rose. Upitala ju je je li to točno, a Rose je potvrdila. Kad su na nju položile ruke, Rose je pala na pod. Kasnije je opisala kako je osjećala **toplinu koja je putovala od grla prema želucu**.

Rose je godinama patila od jakih bolova u želucu i alergija na hranu. Imala je **celijakiju**, bolest prisutnu i u njezinoj obitelji. Nekoliko tjedana nakon te molitve otkrili su da je **potpuno fizički ozdravila**.

**„Sada jede više kruha od mene“**, kaže Monette uz smijeh i dodaje da je to *u Hrvatskoj jako dobra stvar*.
sections.subtitle_en: The “Healing the Whole Person” Conference and a Miraculous Healing from Celiac Disease
sections.screenshot_description_en: Kevin Monette describes the prayer for the physical healing of his wife
sections.content_en:
The search led them to **Dr. Bob Schuchts**. The conference was being held two weeks later, a two-hour drive north of their home, and there were still spots available. They planned the trip and went.

On the second day of the conference, they prayed for **physical healing**. A group of women gathered around Rose. One of them felt a sharp pain in her stomach and thought it might be a pain she was sharing with Rose. She asked her if that was accurate, and Rose confirmed it. When they laid hands on her, Rose fell to the floor. Later she described feeling **a warmth traveling from her throat toward her stomach**.

For years, Rose had suffered from severe stomach pain and food allergies. She had **celiac disease**, an illness also present in her family. A few weeks after that prayer, they discovered that she was **completely physically healed**.

**„Now she eats more bread than I do“**, Monette says with a laugh, adding that *in Croatia that is a very good thing*.

sections.subtitle: Skriveno sjećanje, tri laži i oproštenje zlostavljaču
sections.screenshot_description: Gost nabraja laži koje je njegova supruga desetljećima nosila u sebi
sections.content:
Na istoj konferenciji dogodilo se još nešto. Rose je izronilo **skriveno sjećanje**: kad je imala oko tri godine, seksualno ju je zlostavljao jedan član obitelji.

Počela je prepoznavati uvjerenja koja je od tada nosila u sebi, a Kevin Monette ih nabraja:

- **o sebi**: uvjerenja puna srama, da je loša i prljava;
- **o muškarcima**: da im se ne može vjerovati;
- **o Bogu**: da je On ne može zaštititi i da ju je napustio.

Ta su uvjerenja tijekom života samo jačala. Stvarala su goleme blokade u njezinim odnosima s ljudima i s Bogom, i to **više od trideset godina**, kako naglašava Monette, *„samo zato što je jedan muškarac odlučio biti predator umjesto zaštitnik“*.

Otkriće je bilo golemo za njihov odnos, ali Monette upozorava: **otkriti ranu ne znači iscijeliti je**. Rose je u tom trenutku imala izbor. Mogla se razljutiti i u toj ljutnji ostati, ili se mogla odlučiti za ozdravljenje.

Odabrala je ozdravljenje i **pozvala Isusa u to sjećanje**. Osjetila je Njegovo srce i za sebe i za svog zlostavljača te je **oprostila tom članu obitelji**. Zatim je pronašla Kevina i sve mu ispričala. Zajedno su prošli središnjim prolazom i stali pred oltar zahvaljujući Gospodinu.

Monette zatim još jednom s publikom ponavlja deklaraciju: *„Ljubav nije brzopleta, ne pamti zlo, ne raduje se nepravdi, a raduje se istini.“*
sections.subtitle_en: A Hidden Memory, Three Lies, and Forgiveness to the Abuser
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest lists the lies that his wife carried within herself for decades
sections.content_en:
At the same conference, something else happened. A **hidden memory** surfaced for Rose: when she was about three years old, she was sexually abused by a family member.

She began to recognize beliefs she had carried within herself since then, and Kevin Monette lists them:

- **about herself**: beliefs full of shame, that she was bad and dirty;
- **about men**: that they cannot be trusted;
- **about God**: that He cannot protect her and that He had abandoned her.

Throughout her life, these beliefs only grew stronger. They created enormous blockages in her relationships with people and with God, for **more than thirty years**, as Monette emphasizes, *„just because one man decided to be a predator instead of a protector“*.

The revelation was immense for their relationship, but Monette warns: **discovering a wound does not mean healing it**. Rose had a choice at that moment. She could become angry and stay in that anger, or she could choose healing.

She chose healing and **invited Jesus into that memory**. She felt His heart both for herself and for her abuser, and she **forgave that family member**. Then she found Kevin and told him everything. Together they walked down the center aisle and stood before the altar, thanking the Lord.

Monette then repeats the declaration once more with the audience: *„Love is not hasty, keeps no record of wrongs, does not rejoice in injustice, but rejoices in truth.“*

sections.subtitle: „Ljubav sve pokriva“: otkriti ranu tek je prvi korak
sections.screenshot_description: Kevin Monette objašnjava da je otkrivanje korijena rane samo početak puta ozdravljenja
sections.content:
Posljednja skupina atributa glasi: **ljubav sve pokriva, svemu vjeruje, svemu se nada, sve podnosi**. Publika ponavlja: *„Ja sve pokrivam. Svemu vjerujem. Svemu se nadam. Sve podnosim.“*

Kevin Monette zatim naglašava da je **otkrivanje rane i njezina korijena tek prvi korak**. Ozdravljenja je uvijek još, jer je *Isusova ljubav neprestano dostupna u sve većoj mjeri*.

Otkriva da je i sam na toj konferenciji doživio **radikalno ozdravljenje** i obnovu odnosa sa svojim ocem. O tome, kaže, danas ne može govoriti. Ipak, oboje su s konferencije otišli znajući da su se predali putu ozdravljenja.

Na tom putu bilo je **savjetovanja** te mnogo molitava i susreta **oslobođenja**. Kroz sve to, zaključuje Monette, otkrili su dubinu Božje ljubavi prema njima i težinu onoga što izgovoreno *„da“* u braku doista znači.
sections.subtitle_en: „Love Bears All Things“: Discovering the Wound Is Only the First Step
sections.screenshot_description_en: Kevin Monette explains that discovering the root of the wound is only the beginning of the healing journey
sections.content_en:
The last group of attributes reads: **love bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things**. The audience repeats: *„I bear all things. I believe all things. I hope all things. I endure all things.“*

Kevin Monette then emphasizes that **discovering the wound and its root is only the first step**. There is always more healing, because *Jesus' love is continually available in ever greater measure*.

He reveals that he himself experienced **radical healing** at that conference and the renewal of his relationship with his father. About that, he says, he cannot speak today. Nevertheless, both left the conference knowing they had committed themselves to the journey of healing.

On that journey there was **counseling** and many prayers and encounters of **deliverance**. Through all of that, Monette concludes, they discovered the depth of God's love for them and the weight of what the spoken *„yes“* in marriage truly means.
